measurement: In-process ASGI request elapsed time; includes real providers and DB, excludes local TCP and browser paint

coach_checks.text: Homework stalls when the child gets stuck. They need help asking a clear question.
coach_checks.quality_criterion: Direct help-seeking or learning-question goal; concrete, supported advice.
coach_checks.reply: Try a calm, repeatable prompt: “Show me the part that’s confusing,” then help them turn it into one question, such as “What does this instruction mean?” Let them point, draw, or say it in their own words—no need for a polished question before helping. First check whether they understand the task and have had the teaching they need; if not, clarify or teach that part together.

goals.title: Ask a specific learning question
goals.description: Practice indicating the exact part of a learning activity that needs explanation or support.
goals.reason: Fits the stated need: an adult can scaffold asking about one specific confusing part, without requiring precise wording before offering help.

coach_checks.quality_criterion: Retain the homework topic, lower effort; do not pad with unrelated new goals.
coach_checks.reply: Let them point to the confusing bit—no need to explain it yet. You can ask, “This part?” and then help, or show one example of how to ask: “What does this word mean?” Check first that the directions make sense and the work has been taught. If not, clarify or teach it together. Keep the practice brief and reassuring; asking for help shouldn’t depend on trying and failing first.

goals.title: Ask a specific learning question
goals.description: Practice indicating the exact part of a learning activity that needs explanation or support.
goals.reason: This fits the need to identify one confusing part, while allowing pointing and adult help rather than requiring a polished question.

coach_checks.text: Now a different issue: screen time ends in arguments. We need a realistic stopping point.
coach_checks.quality_criterion: Switch to media stopping or transition support; avoid unrelated homework advice.
coach_checks.reply: Try agreeing on the stopping point before screen time begins: choose a clear event that fits the activity, such as finishing this episode or reaching the next natural save point. Tell your child what happens next, and give a calm reminder before that point. If a game or activity can’t stop easily, choose a more realistic stopping event together. Keep the agreement flexible for accessibility or other family needs.

goals.title: Agree on a realistic media stopping point
goals.description: Before recreational media starts, agree on one feasible stopping event and the support for ending.
goals.reason: This directly supports a realistic, agreed stopping event before recreational media starts, with adult help matched to an eight-year-old.

habit_check.parent_instruction: Use a gesture during homework and avoid extra materials.
